title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1LC1LF_---1LD_1LE0RA_1RE1LB_1RD0LD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1LC1LF_---1LD_1LE0RA_1RE1LB_1RD0LD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open; the machine probably never halts. A marker crawls through a growing block and eats the markers in front of it (proved in Lean); each time it turns into a signal, one long excursion rebuilds the block and part of the tail behind it. Such an excursion can halt the machine, but only when the block and the tail fit exactly: the tape 2^173 1 2^42 1 halts, and the machine itself passed 2^171 1 2^42 1 at step 219,107. An exact accelerated simulation finds no halt in 10300 steps, and the numbers that would have to fit grow by a factor of about 3 per event.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 49,386 cells have been visited and 32,933 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 9.71·10<sup>13</sup> steps (accelerated run)
claims.text: The run-length simulator tools/py/bbtools/rleaccel.py (blocks of 6 cells, runs crossed in one step, and cycle jumps, each used only after its one-cycle rule has been proved symbolically for all lengths; tested cell for cell against direct runs) runs 169,000,000 macro steps from blank tape without a halt. That is more than 9.71·1013 machine steps; the tape then spans 12,705,084 cells.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.512). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Tape structure
claims.text: Read as runs of 1s separated by single 0s, the tape is a list of blocks of 2-runs ((110)^n) separated by marker runs: at 109 steps 1 2^10415 4 2^975 3 2^3848 6 6 2^653 3 2^244 3 2^30 6 2^116 3 2^18 6 2^66 3 2^34 6 2^42 1. The right part from 2^30 on is identical at 108 steps; only the blocks near the growing left end change.

claims.title: The marker crawls through the 2s
claims.text: Mk a b R = 0^inf D> 0 0 (110)^a 1110 (110)^b R: two sweeps take Mk a (b+1) R to Mk (a+3) b R in 24a+70 steps, for all a, b and every tape R; iterated, Mk a (b+j) R reaches Mk (a+3j) b R.

claims.title: The rewriting rules
claims.text: Read as a list of digits (runs of 1s between single 0s), every change between consecutive visits of the left end in the first 3·10<sup>8</sup> steps is one of a few local rules that keep the number of cells: 3 2 → 6 → 2 3 (the marker), 3 3 → 7 → 2 4 → 2 1 (merging and decay), 3 6 → 10 → 2 7, 3 1 → 5 → 2 2, plus fast signals (a 1 crossing a block of 2s in one sweep) and rare epochs where a long block at the left end is rebuilt (N = 2, 8, 214, 1220, 2528, 7645).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>300</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact macro simulation (blocks of 3 cells on a fixed grid, runs of equal blocks crossed at once, linear cycle jumps at the head's turning points under a stated condition that makes them exact) runs to 10300 steps without a halt (py/msim.py run 300, 26 minutes). The C version agrees with the plain machine (state, head, tape hash) at four step counts up to 2·109, with and without jumps at 1013 and 3·1015 steps, and with the Python version (unbounded integers) at 1018 and 1036 steps.

claims.title: Signal events
claims.text: At the visits of the left end the tape is 2^n M TAIL (run lengths) and only the first marker M moves. When it has merged with the next marker and decayed into a signal 1, one long excursion rebuilds the block and the left part of the tail: eight such events up to 4·1010 steps, e.g. 2^52 1 2 1 to 2^4 6 2^28 3 2^14 6 2^8 3 2 1 and 2^171 1 2^42 1 to the full reset 4 2^214.

claims.title: A signal event can halt
claims.text: The plain machine started from 2^173 1 2^42 1 halts after 299,509 steps; from 2^171 1 2^42 1, the machine's own tape at step 219,107, it resets to 4 2^214. Among the 500 tapes 2^n 1 2^b 1 with n = 40..59, b = 0..24, seven halt, n = 4b+3 resets to 4 2^(5b+4) (also for 13 larger n), and the rest are rebuilt. The reset tapes 4 2^5 and 4 2^8 halt; 4 2^2 is the machine's tape at step 59.

claims.title: Halting needs an exact fit, less and less likely
claims.text: A halt (like a full reset) needs an exact relation between the block length n and the first block b of the tail (near n = 4b; of 3,072 tapes with two-block tails 41 halt, almost all on such a line, whatever the second block is). n grows by a factor of about 3 per event, so if the fits behave like chance the probability of a halt per event falls like 1/n and the sum over all events converges: the machine probably never halts.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof of non-halting needs the signal event as an exact map on (n, tail) and an invariant that keeps the run off the halting fits; no halt in 10<sup>300</sup> steps.

check: python3 holdouts/1RB1RF_1LC1LF_---1LD_1LE0RA_1RE1LB_1RD0LD/py/msim.py check     # the accelerated simulator against the plain machine
python3 holdouts/1RB1RF_1LC1LF_---1LD_1LE0RA_1RE1LB_1RD0LD/py/msim.py run 100   # no halt in 10^100 steps

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, but probably not. Started on a blank tape, this machine has not stopped in 10<sup>300</sup> steps (an exact, accelerated simulation). It can stop only in a rare kind of event, and only if two large numbers fit each other exactly; the machine came within two of such a fit after 219,107 steps, and the numbers have been growing ever since.

facts.text: No halt in an exact accelerated simulation.
A marker moves one digit right per two sweeps; the block behind it gains three: proved in Lean.
The tape 2^173 1 2^42 1 halts; the machine itself passed 2^171 1 2^42 1.
A halt needs an exact fit between numbers that triple at every event.

sections.heading: A list of digits, and markers crawling through it
html: Write the tape as runs of 1s separated by single 0s, and write each run as its length. The tape becomes a list of digits, almost all 2s, with a few markers:
(2^7645 means 7645 twos in a row.) The head sweeps over the whole list and back; each round trip adds a digit at the left end.

<svg viewBox='0 0 560 130' role='img' aria-label='the marker 3 becomes 6 and then moves one digit right' style='width:100%;max-width:560px;height:auto;font:13px var(--mono)'><g fill='var(--fg)'><text x='10' y='25'>sweep 1:</text><text x='110' y='25'>2 2 2 <tspan fill='var(--head)' font-weight='700'>3</tspan> 2 2 2 2</text><text x='10' y='65'>sweep 2:</text><text x='110' y='65'>2 2 2 <tspan fill='var(--head)' font-weight='700'>6</tspan> 2 2 2</text><text x='10' y='105'>sweep 3:</text><text x='110' y='105'>2 2 2 2 <tspan fill='var(--head)' font-weight='700'>3</tspan> 2 2 2</text></g><text x='330' y='65' fill='var(--muted)'>111 0 11 = 111111 = 11 0 111</text></svg>

A marker 3 moves one digit right every two sweeps, passing through the form 6 (the same six cells with the 0 filled in). This motion is proved in Lean for blocks of any length. When a marker catches the next one they merge and decay: 3 3 → 7 → 2 4 → 2 2 1; a 1 is a fast signal that crosses a whole block of 2s in a single sweep and becomes a new marker at its end. Every rule keeps the number of cells.

Every so often a long block at the left end is rebuilt at once (an epoch); the block sizes at the epochs are 2, 8, 214, 1220, 2528, 7645. What decides them is not yet understood, so there is no map from one epoch to the next, and no estimate of whether the machine halts.

Where it could halt

Only by arriving at the blank left end of the tape in state B. In the run the head always arrives there in state D, E or F.

sections.heading: Signals rebuild the tape, and can stop the machine
html: Seen at the moments the head reaches a new leftmost cell, the tape is a long block of 2s, one moving marker, and a tail of further blocks and markers that stand still. The marker crawls right, the block behind it grows, and when the marker reaches the next one the two merge and decay into a single 1: a signal. Then the head stays away from the left end for a long time, and when it comes back the block has been cut into pieces:

<svg viewBox='0 0 600 120' role='img' aria-label='a signal event: block and tail before, rebuilt tape after' style='width:100%;max-width:600px;height:auto;font:12px var(--mono)'><text x='4' y='14' fill='var(--muted)'>before (step 17,074)</text><rect x='4' y='20' width='416' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='212' y='35' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>2^52</text><rect x='420' y='20' width='14' height='22' fill='var(--head)'/><text x='427' y='56' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--head)'>1</text><rect x='434' y='20' width='16' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><rect x='450' y='20' width='8' height='22' fill='var(--accent)'/><text x='4' y='78' fill='var(--muted)'>after (step 31,483)</text><rect x='4' y='84' width='32' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><rect x='36' y='84' width='8' height='22' fill='var(--accent)'/><rect x='44' y='84' width='224' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='156' y='99' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>2^28</text><rect x='268' y='84' width='8' height='22' fill='var(--accent)'/><rect x='276' y='84' width='112' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='332' y='99' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>2^14</text><rect x='388' y='84' width='8' height='22' fill='var(--accent)'/><rect x='396' y='84' width='64' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><text x='428' y='99' text-anchor='middle' fill='var(--bg)'>2^8</text><rect x='460' y='84' width='8' height='22' fill='var(--accent)'/><rect x='468' y='84' width='8' height='22' fill='var(--ink)'/><rect x='476' y='84' width='6' height='22' fill='var(--accent)'/></svg>

Eight such events happen in the first 4·1010 steps, each about three times larger than the one before. Most just rebuild the tape. But the event can also end in two other ways, when the block and the tail fit exactly:

• Full reset: a block of 4b+3 with a tail of one block of b becomes the tape 4 2^(5b+4), with nothing else on it. The machine did this once: 2^171 1 2^42 1 at step 219,107 (171 = 4·42 + 3).
  • Halt: 2^173 1 2^42 1, two more 2s in the block, halts after 299,509 steps. So do a handful of other exact fits.

So the machine once came within two digits of halting. Since then the block has grown to astronomical sizes, and an exact accelerated simulation shows no halt in 10300 steps. If the fits happen by chance, the chance per event shrinks like one over the size of the block, and the total chance that is left is tiny. Nobody has turned this into a proof.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.512). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 49,386 cells (33,922 left of the start, 163 right), with a density of 1s of 0.667.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A marker crawls through a growing block of 2s (runs of two 1s) and eats the markers in front of it; each time it becomes a signal, one long excursion rebuilds the tape, and it ends in a halt or a full reset only when block and tail fit exactly (2^173 1 2^42 1 halts; the run passed 2^171 1 2^42 1); exact accelerated run: no halt in 10<sup>300</sup> steps; open.
family: marker crawling through blocks of 2s, signal events that rebuild the tape
